HISTORY LYCEUM OF THE PHILIPPINES UNIVERSITY prides itself with its long and rich tradition of Academic Excellence through the legacy of its founder, Dr. Jose P. Laurel. The only Philippine President to have served in all three branches of the Government, Dr. Laurel was a successful lawyer, legislator, constitutionalist, jurist, writer, scholar, statesman, philosopher, and above all things, an educator. Dr. Laurel’s concern for education was his most abiding passion. A graduate of top educational institutions such as University of the Philippines College of Law, Escuela de Derecho, University of Santo Tomas, and Yale University, his credentials as an educator were unassailable. He wrote extensively on education and managed to teach in several educational institutions in Manila, despite his numerous commitments. During the Second World War, as the leader of the nation during the darkest period in its history, he introduced educational policies that emphasized and upheld national morale and character. As a senator after the war, he authored the law creating the National Education Board alongside Sen. Claro M. Recto. The inspiration to establish a University came to him in the early 1920’s while a student at Yale. Three decades later, along with some of his close friends, he turned this dream into a reality. With the aim of becoming a center of academic excellence in the Philippines and the Far East, Lyceum of the Philippines University (then still a college) formally opened its doors to the public on July 7, 1952. With his admiration for knowledge and his appreciation of classical thought, Dr. Laurel named the school Lyceum of the Philippines after Lykeios, the site in ancient Athens where the great philosopher Aristotle nurtured the minds of his protégées. The school’s motto, Veritas et Fortitudo, Pro Deo et Patria, reflects Dr. Laurel’s belief in the value of learning and character formation for God and country. Unfortunately, Dr. Laurel unexpectedly died in 1959 while at work. On his third son, Sotero, who was then in the practice of law, fell the mantle of responsibility of running the school. He was the natural choice as, in years earlier; it was Senator Sotero who helped his father organize Lyceum and acted as the first executive secretary to his father, the school President, before resuming his law practice. For the next forty–three years, it was this chosen son, Sotero, who nurtured the school and made it grow beyond Manila into the provinces. In 1966, he founded the Lyceum of the Philippines University–Batangas followed by Lyceum of the Philippines University–Laguna in 2000. Both campuses are now headed by Senator Laurel’s fourth son, Peter, who was elected President in 2000. In 2008, the Cavite Campus was established to bring the total number of LPU campuses to four with a grand total enrollment of approximately 25,000 students, about 10,000 of whom are enrolled in various hospitality courses. As of Academic Year 2011 –2012, LPU Cavite has an enrollment of almost 7,000 students and further taking a major leap forward in enrollment, facilities and quality instruction. Senator Laurel’s eldest son, Atty. Roberto Laurel, heads the Manila and Cavite Campuses as President. History 6

II. STUDENT RIGHTS AND RESPONSIBILITIES STUDENT RIGHTS Subject to the limitations prescribed by the laws of the land, students shall enjoy the following rights: 1. The right to quality and relevant education through competent and continuing instruction 2. The right to organize, join and participate in organizations and societies ac- credited by the University 3. The right to guidance and counseling services 4. The right to freedom of expression and assembly, subject to such constraints as to ensure the proper exercise and enjoyment of the same freedom by all members of the academic community and the uninterrupted pursuit of LPU’s mission as an institution of higher learning 5. The right to invite resource persons during assemblies, symposia, and other activities of similar nature, in accordance with prescribed procedures subject to conditions laid down by the University to ensure good order and the achievement of its policies and objectives as an institution of higher learning, and provided such activities do not interfere with or disrupt classroom instruction or any other academic activities of the University 6. The right of access through authorized channels to their student records/ grades and to be issued transfer credentials, official certificates and transcripts of records STUDENT RESPONSIBILITIES Students are invested with the following obligations and responsibilities: 1. To study conscientiously and achieve the best possible academic performance 2. To uphold the basic principles and ideals of the University and contribute to the attainment of its objectives 3. To exercise their rights in a responsible manner with due regard for the rights of others 4. To preserve the academic atmosphere by observing discipline and by maintaining harmonious relationships with administrative and academic officials, faculty members, non-teaching personnel, security personnel and fellow students 5. To abide by all University rules and regulations as stated in this Handbook 13

LPU STATEMENT OF STUDENT ACADEMIC RESPONSIBILITY Lyceum of the Philippines University is committed to the development of a complete and lasting educational experience for its students which promotes the fundamental University core values of Love of God, Probity, Unity, Nationalism, Justice, Pro -Environment, and Leadership (LPUNJPL). Consequently, this statement on Student Academic Responsibility addresses some principles of student conduct and behavior expected of responsible, competent, and ethical graduates. Observing these fundamental guidelines will result in responsible and ethical LPU graduates. 14

CLASSROOM DECORUM It is expected that students will demonstrate a professional attitude toward quality learning throughout their course of study. With respect to classroom decorum, students should support and promote the creation of a positive and excellent learning environment. To reach this desired learning environment, LPU students are expected to be responsible participants and are required to: 1. Attend all classes (except for sickness, personal or family tragedy or formal excuse) 2. Come to class on time 3. Stand and greet the teachers as they enter the classroom 4. Recite the LPU Opening Prayer and LPU Closing Prayer 5. Maintain the cleanliness and orderliness of the classroom by practicing 6S 6. Come to class prepared by having fully completed their assignments 7. Actively engage in the classroom experience 8. Treat the class as a professional experience 9. Dress in appropriate attire 10. Respect the views of other students 11. Respect the professor’s prerogative to establish reasonable class standards 12. Observe good manners and right conduct inside the campus (show courtesy, greet all teachers and other officials, no public display of affection, self–discipline, etc.) LPU students must also refrain from any behavior which might interfere with the instructor’s ability to conduct the class or disrupt the ability of other students to learn. Likewise, students must observe the following inside the classroom: 1. Avoid the inappropriate use of electronic devices; 2. Abstain from eating without permission; 3. Refrain from unnecessary conversation during class; and 4. Resist the urge to leave class without cause. LPU students must realize that their individual attitude contributes significantly to the collective learning in the classroom. We expect LPU students to internalize a classroom culture that fosters an intellectual and professional learning environment. We remind that LPU students abide by the policies set forth in LPU documents and, therefore, accept the personal responsibility needed to become skilled professionals, reasonable community leaders, and proud graduates. 15

H. GRADING 1. GRADING SYSTEM 1.1. A final grade report shall be issued at the end of each academic term. 1.2. All subjects offered in LPU will use grade points as final marks, except FDA (Failure Due to Absences), DRP (Dropped), NA (Never Appeared), and INC (incomplete). 1.3. Students who are not able to take the final examinations or are notable to submit the final requirement in a subject shall be given a grade of in- complete (INC). 1.4. LPU adopts the following grade point system with the following percent - age equivalents and descriptions: GRADE POINTS PERCENTAGE EQUIVALENT GENERAL DESCRIPTION 1.00 99–100% Excellent 1.25 96–98 Outstanding 1.50 93–95 Superior 1.75 90–92 Very Good 2.00 87–89 Good 2.25 84–86 Satisfactory 2.50 81–83 Fairly Satisfactory 2.75 78–80 Fair 3.00 75–77 Passed 5.00 Below 75 Failed Other Marks: “FDA” “NA” “DRP” (Failure Due to Absences) (Never Appeared) (Dropped) “INC” (Incomplete) 2. BASES OF GRADES 2.1. The following factors shall be considered in the computation of grades: 2.1.1. Preliminary Period Grade - 33.33% 2.1.2. Midterm Period Grade - 33.33.% 2.1.3. Final Period Grade - 33.34% 2.1.4. Final Grade - sum of all the period grades 2.2. Each grading period is composed of the following: Class performance = 60% Major Exam = 40% 2.3. A final grade with a percentage equivalent which has an excess of 0.5 shall automatically rounded off to the nearest whole number (Example: 84.5 should be rounded off to 85). After which, the grade point is deter- mined. (Example: 86.5 should be rounded off first to 87; 87 is therefore equivalent to 2.00) 39

3. GENERAL POLICIES ON GRADING 3.1. The final grade shall be computed according to the official formula in the computation of grades. 3.2. In addition to Practicum/OJT and Research/Thesis/Feasibility Study/Project Design/Capstone, the grade of “INC” shall be givento students who will not be able to take the final examination. 3.3. Thesis subjects shall be graded as presented on schedule. Oral defense for undergraduate theses shall be done by the student(s) before members of the panel. The final grade shall be given by the faculty handling the thesis/ research/feasibility/ project study/ capstone subject. 3.4. All completion tests/examinations must be scheduled within the pre -scribed period. Students who fail to take completion examinations as scheduled shall be automatically given a transmuted grade of 40% for the missed examination. If completion was processed beyond the deadline of the encoding of grades, the Registrar’s Office’s authorized staff shall be responsible in encoding the final completion grade. 3.5. For subjects dropped before midterm examinations, a student shall be marked “Dropped” in the grading sheet, provided there is compliance with the following requirements: 3.5.1. The dropping form duly signed by the instructor/professor concerned and approved by the Dean must be filed with the Registrar’s Office on or before the first day of the midterm examinations. 3.5.2. The dropping form must be filed before the student exceeds the maximum allowable absences as provided for in this Handbook. 3.6. The student secures a clearance from the Dean of Student Affairs along with the approval of the College Dean/Chairperson, and complies with the following requirements: 3.6.1. Any concern regarding final grades may be entertained by the College not later than the succeeding regular semester. 40

4. COMPUTATION FOR THE GRADE POINT AVERAGE The computation of grade point average (GPA) in all credited subjects shall be as follows: 4.1. Credit units for each subject are multiplied by the grade earned toobtain the credit point per subject. 4.2. The resulting credit points are added. 4.3. The total number of credit points is divided by the total number of credit units to obtain the GPA. The GPA is then computed to two (2) decimal places. 4.4. For GPA computation purposes, a descriptive grade of Failure Due to Absences (FDA) or Never Appeared in any subject is equivalent to 5.00. 4.5. Dropped (DRP) or Incomplete (INC) remarks shall not be included in the computation of the GPA. 4.6. Grades in NSTP shall not be included in the computation of the GPA. I. Provisions Against Sexual Harassment 1.5.1. Lyceum of the Philippines University is committed to the prevention of sexual harassment of any member of the LPU community. 1.5.2. Sexual harassment refers to any unwanted sexual attention that is explicitly or implicitly made as a condition for favorable decisions affecting one’s university standing, or which creates an intimidating, hostile, or offensive environment in the university. 1.5.3. Cases of sexual harassment are covered by the implementing guidelines of the Anti –Sexual Harassment Act of 1995 and Safe Spaces Act, R.A. An ad hoc committee will conduct the investigation of alleged cases constituting sexual harassment and will recommend any course of action that may be called for by the investigation. 2. PREVENTIVE SUSPENSION This involves the temporary exclusion of a student from the University premises or any part thereof for the purpose of avoiding or minimizing imminent or continuing danger to the whole or part of the academic community. 2.1. Preventive Suspension from Classroom 2.1.1. A faculty member may dismiss a student for the duration of the class for unruly behavior or acts disruptive of classroom instruction. 2.1.2. A faculty member may, with the approval of the Dean, summarily dismiss a student from his/her class for a maximum of three (3) class hours if, in his opinion, there is imminent or continuing danger of disruptions arising from the student’s continued presence. Preventive suspension beyond three (3) class hours requires the approval of the Executive Director for Academic Affairs / Vice President for Administration. 2.2. Preventive Suspension from the University Premises 2.2.1. A student who poses an imminent or continuing threat to University safety may be temporarily barred from the University premises by the Director of Center for Student Affairs, upon the recommendation of the Chief of Security, with the concurrence of the College Dean, for a maximum period of three (3) class days during the regular semester or two (2) class days during the summer term. Suspension beyond this period requires the approval of the Vice President for Administration. 1.1.1. The period of preventive suspension shall be deducted from any penalty 62

of suspension that may later be imposed on the student. 1.1.2. In both cases, the commission of the offense is recorded in the CSA. 3.2. University/Campus Work This measure allows an erring student to have an opportunity to work either inside or outside the University, depending on the decision of the hearing officer and/or the members of the BOD. University work will be deployed by CSA in coordination with certain departments concerned. 3.3. Suspension This involves barring a student from a particular class or from the school for a prescribed period. Suspension for more than five days will require the approval of the Vice President for Administration. Suspension is considered as absence voluntarily incurred. 3.4. Non–Readmission This measure allows an erring student to finish the semester but thereafter excludes him from enrolling in the University in the undergraduate, graduate, and college of law levels. This shall be meted out when a student commits a major offense with a sanction of non –readmission and based upon the recommendation of the Board of Discipline. The Certification of Good Moral Character will not be issued to the student. 3.5. Exclusion This penalty allows the University to immediately exclude or drop the name of an undesirable student from the University rolls and issue him transfer credentials. This measure shall be taken only against students guilty of major offense/s with a sanction of exclusion and when circumstances of extreme urgency necessitate his/her immediate exclusion. The Certification of Good Moral Character will not be issued to the student. 63

3.6. Expulsion This is the extreme penalty on an erring student which consists of his exclusion for admission to any public or private school in the Philippines; this requires the prior approval of the Commission on Higher Education (CHED). The Certification of Good Moral Character will not be issued to the student. 3.7. Stiffer Penalty A stiffer penalty shall be imposed on students found guilty of repeated violations of the provisions of the Student Handbook. 4. ISSUANCE OF CERTIFICATION OF GOOD MORAL CHARACTER 4.1. The Certification of Good Moral Character (CGMC) is issued upon request to any student who is/was enrolled in LPU Cavite for at least one semester, and who has no derogatory record as set by the guidelines found in this Student Handbook. 4.2. The CGMC will not be issued to: 4.2.1. a student who has committed a Less Serious Offense and/or a Serious Offense punishable by university/community work and has not fully complied with the required sanction. (Upon the approval of the Head of CSA, the CGMC may be issued to the student after he/she has finished the required number of hours for university / community work.) 4.2.2. a student who has committed a Serious Offense punishable by suspension. 4.2.3. a student who has committed a Very Serious Offense. J. ACADEMIC GRIEVANCE PROCEDURE An academic grievance is a result of a dispute or conflict in the learning process or in the performance of a student in an academic program. Only queries from the student or the parent/guardian indicated in the SPR and pertaining to the academic performance or status of the student in an academic program will be entertained. In the same way, if there is a dispute or conflict in the learning process or in the academic performance of the student that needs to be clarified, only the parent/guardian who is indicated in the Student’s Personal Records (SPR) will accompany him/her. An academic grievance may be formal or informal. An academic grievance made orally is informal in nature. When the grievance is written and duly signed and sworn in, it then becomes formal. Only formal academic grievances will be given due course. 1. The formal complaint against a faculty member can be filed anytime within the semester but not later than two (2) weeks after the start of the following semester. A complaint must be duly notarized before submission to the Chair of the program/ department. 64

2. The student–complainant must submit three (3) copies of his/her complaint; these copies are for the department, faculty concerned, and the student. 3. A formal student grievance filed against a faculty member will initially go through a preliminary hearing involving the following: 3.1. Student 3.2. Faculty concerned 3.3. The Dean/Chairperson of the College/Department where the faculty belongs 4. Upon receipt of the complaint, together with all supporting documents, the College Dean / Department Chairpersons shall require the respondent to answer the complaint in writing within five (5) days from the receipt of the complaint. The decision of the Dean / Chairperson is effective immediately. The student/complainant, however, has five (5) days to appeal the decision of the Chairperson; otherwise, he/she has waived his/her right to appeal. 5. The office of the Vice President for Academic Affairs (VPAA) is the venue particular to an appeal regarding an academic grievance. The VPAA convenes the College Academic Grievance Committee for the purpose. The Committee is composed of the following: 5.1. the Dean of College where the faculty belongs 5.2. A member of the College, preferably from the same department where the faculty concerned belongs 5.3. President of LYCESGO or his/her authorized representative 6. The Committee shall conduct at least one (1) hearing before deciding a case. The Committee can call for witnesses, request for documents, and invite resource persons to aid them in the disposition of the case. 7. The decision of the Committee is the decision of the College. However, the student – complainant can appeal the decision of the College at the Vice President for Administration level within five (5) days from its promulgation. The VPAA/VPA either concurs with the decision of the College or forwards the case to the College Academic Grievance Committee on the strength of new evidence or possible misinterpretation of any rule or regulation. The decision of the VPAA/VPA is final. 65
